# NOTES: Compaction of "Theophano: The Crusade of the Tenth Century" (Frederic Harrison, 1904, Gutenberg #79024)

Single novel, no separate books. Sections are numbered chapters I–XXXIII with titles, plus "THE END."

## Ch I: The Boy Basileus (956)
- Hunt on Mount Damatrys (Bulgarlu), Asian side of Bosphorus, near Chrysopolis (Scutari), at Constantine VII Porphyrogennetus's reign's close. Spring dawn, year 956.
- Young Romanus (son of Constantine), gored by wild boar in thigh. Huntsmen bring him to woodman's hut, then house of **Craterus the Laconian** (Spartan descent, ruined by Saracen corsairs, foxlike sinister eyes, white beard). Daughter **Anastasia** (Greek goddess beauty, sapphire eyes), veiled, tends him with old nurse **Charmion** and maid. Tourniquet applied.
- Romanus, faint, kisses Anastasia's hand; gives her a ring (emerald set in enamel, inscription). Says "Let not my father know."
- Craterus warns daughter to forget youth. Anastasia recalls mother's Spartan royal blood; Craterus rants about Mithras, Isis, Athene, Saracens, "Basil the stable-boy."
- Anastasia has Charmion take ring to engraver **Leontius**: inscription reads "Κυρει Βοηθει Ρωμανω" (Lord, help Romanus / Romans). Anastasia resolves to be Augusta.

## Ch II: The Warden of the Eastern March
- Party rows barge to Constantinople. Leader **Basil Digenes** (Akritas, warden of eastern march; son of Syrian emir **Mousur** of Edessa and Eudocia Ducas; dark, fiery, Persian-hilted weapon). Companion **Theodore**, the chamberlain (*parakeimomenos*-type courtier, scheming).
- Theodore urges Basil to think of succession; Basil refuses throne, names **Nicephorus Phocas** (commander Asia) as the true savior. Theodore drops subject.
- Description of Bosphorus, Golden Horn, walls of Constantinople, Princes' Isles, Mount Olympus of Bithynia.

## Ch III: The Betrothal
- Shrine of St Demetrius on Asian shore. Anastasia summoned by note. Romanus kisses her, offers palace. She sobs: "Our Lady of Mount Damatrys." She demands oath: "I, Romanus, take thee, Anastasia, for my wedded wife." Swears on icon.
- Hermit-priest (secretly the patriarch-linked hermit) pronounces betrothal. Anastasia escapes with Charmion.
- Romanus confides to chamberlain Theodore, who fears the hermit's link to Patriarch **Polyeuctus**; Theodore sees opportunity to rule through Theophano-to-be.

## Ch IV: The Young Augusta
- Russian envoys from Olga (Kiev). Banquet in Chrysotriklinos. Emperor Constantine dying. Empress Helena; daughter **Agatha** (youngest).
- Theophano (Anastasia renamed), presented by Euphemia (wife of Theodore). Emperor delighted. Reads from *Book of Ceremonies* (*Basileia Taxis*) on imperial marriage rite.
- Marriage of Romanus and Theophano. Children: Basil (future Basil II, "Slayer of Bulgarians") and Constantine (future Constantine VIII). Romanus's debauchery; polo with Digenes; Theophano tolerates.

## Ch V: The Dying Emperor
- Constantine's council: Patriarch Polyeuctus (denounces Theophano, cites Jezebel/Ahab), **Joseph Bringas** (eunuch, parakeimomenos, chief minister), Sisinnios (prefect), Theophylact Matzitzikos (chief secretary), Judge Joseph. They praise Nicephorus. Emperor fears him.
- Constantine dies in November (Romanus hunting, absent). Theophano bars Augusta Helena from chamber: "There is no Augusta here but one."

## Ch VI: The Coronation (960)
- Eric, Norwegian Varangian recruit, with general **Bardas Skleros**, tours troops (Dyrrhachian Highlanders, Patzinaks, Russ, Armenians) at Hebdomon. Describes Theodosian walls.
- Procession: Varangians, clergy, Patriarch, Bringas (parakeimomenos), Nicephorus (Armenian, 46, in worn tunic). Romanus II coronated; Theophano crowned. Hippodrome games (Blues, Greens). Consecration in St Sophia.

## Ch VII: The Confession
- Eric sees Nicephorus confessing to monk **Athanasius** (earlier Abraham, nephew of Maleinos). Nicephorus resigns, to enter hermitage on Mount Olympus. Confesses lust for Theophano ("Vulcan," Theophano mocked him). Athanasius penance: return to Anatolian marches, no contact with her. Nicephorus accepts.

## Ch VIII: The Sacred Palace
- Romanus's debauchery; Bringas installed as minister. Glaucus of Miletus (Samian governor's son) tells of Saracen sack of Miletus; Crete (Chandax) the base.
- Romanus refuses to send Nicephorus to Crete; Bringas insists. Princesses (Zoe, Theodora, Anna, Theophano-sisters, Agatha) demand protection. Monk **John** of Stoudion orders them to convent. Dowager Helena protests. Theophano threatens to take veil; princesses dragged to convents.

## Ch IX: The Muster of the Crusade (July 960)
- Fleet of 360 vessels; 123 dromons; 57,890 men (per deacon Theodosius). Flagship *Archangel Michael*. Greek fire.
- Nicephorus blessed by Polyeuctus; Theophano whispers "master of Rome."
- Princesses Anna, Agatha in convent of Myrelaeon (Canicleion). Agatha refuses vows. Digenes rescues Agatha through confessor disguise, to Proconnesus (sister Theodosia, wife of George Comnenus).

## Ch X: The Conquest of Crete
- Emir **Abd-el-Aziz** (kouropas), governor. Prisoners tortured (Chian seamen, Thessalonian landsman). Nicephorus prays, harangues troops. Landing, Varangian shield-wall, cataphracti.
- Pastilas killed in ambush. Siege of Chandax. "Witch of Nejd" crone, shot by Mongol archer.

## Ch XI: The Storming of Chandax
- Digenes captured by Saracens, dungeon, wounded (left shoulder). Emir's daughter **Fatima** (Ben-Senoussi's daughter; Nubian nurse), sees resemblance to her brother Hassan (Digenes nursed Hassan at death). Fatima frees him; she is his cousin (both from Mousour/Edessa family line).
- Envoys from Abd-er-Rahman III (Cordova). Mine under walls; Chandax falls; Ben-Senoussi killed by Nicephorus. Massacre. Digenes rescued by Nicephorus from Tartars.

## Ch XII: Digenes and Fatima
- Booty auction; slaves. Girl **Zoe/Zainab** from Melos. Nicephorus appoints Digenes to lead embassy to Cordova, returning captives including Fatima. Fatima hints at conversion; Digenes says Agatha is his beloved; Fatima withdraws in despair.

## Ch XIII: The Caliph of the West
- Embassy at Cordova: Bardas Skleros, Eric, poet-deacon Theodosius, protocolist Michael, Fatima. Ibn Khaldun (librarian), vizier Ahmed. Caliph Abd-er-Rahman III dies; son Hakim II succeeds. Hakim tells of his brother Abdallah bowstrung; father's note: "fourteen days truly happy."

## Ch XIV: The Conquest of Aleppo (963 onward)
- Nicephorus at Caesarea; Romanus pressed command eastern armies. Theophano seduces Nicephorus ("Sibyl"). Tactics book quoted. Bringas tries to sideline him with John Tzimisces. Campaign through Taurus, Cilicia, Aleppo (Seif Eddauleh/Chamdas). Aleppo falls Christmas 962/963.
- Missive: Augusta will be widowed in three months.

## Ch XV: Empress and Chamberlain (March 963)
- Romanus dies after hunt (boar; wine). Theophano at deathbed; forced will making her regent; pen guided to sign. Patriarch Polyeuctus intervenes. Senate compromise: Theophano regent for sons Basil II and Constantine VIII; Bringas retained.
- Bringas plans to blind Nicephorus; Nicephorus enters council, is saved by Theophano's arrival. Triumph in Hippodrome with St John's tunic relic. Nicephorus kneels to Theophano.

## Ch XVI: Caesar at the Rubicon
- Nicephorus flees to church of Holy Wisdom for sanctuary; mob defends him. Polyeuctus forces him into senate; he swears loyalty. Stephanus Lecapenus found dead at Lesbos (Easter). Bringas letter orders John Tzimisces and Courcouas to seize him; they proclaim him Augustus at Cappadocia. "Nicephorus had crossed his Rubicon."

## Ch XVII: The New Basileus (August 963)
- Acclamation at Caesarea; march to Bosphorus. Bringas holds city with Apambas; Basil Lecapenus (illegitimate, eunuch) leads revolt; Apambas killed by vase. Nicephorus crowned in Holy Wisdom (Aug 16). Digenes in palace.

## Ch XVIII: Emperor and Patriarch
- Nicephorus's ascetic reign; hair-shirt; Bardas made Caesar; Basil Lecapenus president of senate; Leo curopalates; Bringas exiled. Theophano moved to Petrion, then marries Nicephorus. Polyeuctus refuses entry to sanctuary; bishop of Caesarea argues the canon was iconoclast; Stylianos plot about godfather status. Festivals.

## Ch XIX: The Saracen Peril
- Nicephorus plans Syria; Digenes dialogue. Sicily expedition to Rametta: Manuel (cousin) and Nicetas fail; Manuel killed at Rametta.

## Ch XX: An Emperor's Day
- Review ground; Eric learns tactics from Bardas. Embassies: Ghalib, Ibn Khaldun, Italians, Bulgarians. Nicephorus refuses Czar Peter's "tribute" demand; war declared on Bulgaria.

## Ch XXI: Islam and Cross
- Abd-el-Aziz on Prote island. Daughter **Sophia** (converted, nun-educated). Son **Anemas** sent to Kairouan (Al-Muizz) then Cordova to meet Fatima. Fatima refuses Anemas; says "one God."

## Ch XXII: The Stars in Their Courses
- Astrologer Aaron Ben Ammon (Jewish) cast horoscopes; recognizes Theophano (earlier Anastasia). Gives poisons; killed by Psellus. Theophano plans to remove Digenes; Agatha forced to marry Sisinnios; Digenes drugged; Theophano attempts seduction; Nicephorus interrupts.

## Ch XXIII: The March on Antioch (965–966)
- Beacon telegraph; Leo the historian and Joannes the geometer. Nicephorus sends Theophano to Drizibion. Mad prophet Daniel of Olympus prophesies Theophano's fate.

## Ch XXIV: Love and Falsehood
- Joannes reports Tzimisces's treachery; intercepted Armenian message "From the prison of Drizibion." Nicephorus confronts Theophano; she denies. Tzimisces denies. Nicephorus never smiles again.

## Ch XXV: Love and Troth
- Digenes nursed by Agatha and Theodosia Comnena; physicians Theophanes Nonnos and Synesios. Digenes raves of Fatima; Agatha jealous. Fatima marrying Anemas plans noted. Digenes leaves for camp; they part forever.

## Ch XXVI: Old Rome (Christmas 967)
- Otto I crowns son Otto II; Pope John XIII. Byzantine visitors Michael, Joannes, Symeon, Alexios, Guido of Bari. Bishop Luitprand of Cremona. Gerbert of Aurillac at council; Otto's embassy to Byzantium.

## Ch XXVII: Old Rome and New Rome
- Otto attacks Bari; Digenes defends. Luitprand insulted at Constantinople; Nicephorus rebukes him. Pandulph of Capua defeated at Bovinum: Digenes and Pandulph kill each other in single combat. Agatha becomes nun.

## Ch XXVIII: Basileus in Council
- Nicephorus's law reforms: monastery gifts restricted; military fiefs; abbot Anthony of Stoudion protests. Nicephorus wants martyrdom for holy warriors; Athanasius refuses. Nicephorus plans Theophano's removal to Prote; Athanasius forbids divorce.

## Ch XXIX: The Rising Storm
- Tax crisis, new *tetarteron* coin; wall around palace; Boucoleon fortified. Riots; Elias of Stoudion sermon. Stone-throwing at Nicephorus; women burned. Hippodrome panic kills many.

## Ch XXX: The Last Campaign
- Nicephorus takes Antioch-region cities, Emesa, Jerusalem attacked; Bardas Phocas dies. Leo reports Theophano plotting with Tzimisces; Nicephorus confronts Tzimisces, places him under arrest.

## Ch XXXI: The Last Agony
- Nicephorus's grief; Leo, Zachariah the confessor reproaches. Nicephorus prays to Mary before icon; Theophano visits; he sleeps on panther skin.

## Ch XXXII: Clytemnestra
- Storm night (969). Theophano hides Bourtzes and Balantes; four bravos disguised as maids. Captain of guard searches; Theophano bathes. Icon of Christ broken; Tzimisces arrives by basket. Nicephorus murdered in sleep (struck, beaten, head severed; head hung from window). Varangians refuse to avenge a corpse.

## Ch XXXIII: Retribution
- Tzimisces crowned; patriarch Polyeuctus refuses to crown with Theophano; Theophano strikes child Basil. Tzimisces exiles her to a convent on a Euxine island. "The evil one is put away from Rome forever."

**END OF TEXT**
